text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's government has to close loss-making state firms and provide incentives for the private companies that make a profit, the International Monetary Fund's mission leader Anne McGuirk said before leaving Bulgaria.
The mission has not demanded new tax hikes, she added, rejecting local media reports.
-- The Socialist majority in parliament overruled President Zhelyu Zhelev's veto on the Radio and Television Law and approved it without amendments.

-- Bulgaria's main opposition Union of Democratic Forces is expected to discuss next week whether to submit a no-confidence motion against the socialist government over its economic and social policies, opposition deputies said.

-- The cabinet decided that Kremikovtsi steel works could receive short-term credits of up to $11 million but it would not be taken off the government's list of firms that were banned from new loans until they collect their debts, Industry minister Lyubomir Dachev said.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet decided to impose maximum price limits on basic foods by September 12 in a bid to curb soaring inflation boosted by a weakening lev and economic instability, Agriculture minister Krastyo Trendafilov said.
-- Bulgaria's central government budget deficit rose by 2.7 billion levs in the second half of August to 72.4 billion levs or 89.7 percent of 1996 target, finance ministry figures show.

-- The cabinet approved the sale of a 75-percent stake in the debt-ridden Plama oil refinery, initially slated for liquidation, to Bulgaria's Euroenergy holding, Privatisation Agency's executive director Vesselin Blagoev said.
-- Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency said it has sold 55 percent of the indebted Lovech-based electric tool maker Eltos to the Berlin-registered Sparki Trading GmbH for 11.5 million German marks.
-- Police in Sofia defused two hand-made bombs planted at the city's central railway station, the Interior Ministry said. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
